To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

aortic systolic blood pressure (aSBP), measured with a validated oscillometric method and assessed with mean and diastole pressure calibration, independently predicted mortality in a chronic kidney cohort and that this prognostic value was significantly increased by adding office brachial SBPs.
aSBP, assessed with measured mean pressure and diastolic blood pressure, is a strong predictor of mortality in patients with chronic kidney disease stages II–IV.

aortic systolic blood pressure, calibrated using measured mean and distolic blood pressure, predicts all cause mortality in chronic kidney disease stages2–4, and that this association is independent of brachial systoic blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calibration issue of aSBP and its association to cardiovascular outcome, which has not yet been sufficiently investigated.
the question, if aSBP is a better predictor of mortality than bSBP, or if aSBP can be assessed with sufficient accuracy to be of clinical value.
the question whether aortic SBP is superior to brachial SBPs for the prediction of cardiovascular events and mortality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bSBP and mean arterial pressure are of limited use for aortic SBP assessment.
aortic SBP, calibrated with brachial mean blood pressure, is an independent prognostic factor of all-cause mortality.
aSBP is a strong predictor of mortality, and that the method of calibration has an important impact on its prognostic value.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method of calibration of aSBP is crucial for its prognostic value.
bSBP is not sufficient to predict cardiovascular mortality in CKD patients and that aSBP assessed by a calibrated method is superior to bSBP in predicting mortality in this patient population.
aortic pressure is an independent predictor for all-cause mortality and that the method of calibration is important.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method of calibration is of importance and needs to be considered for future studies.
aortic pressure should be calibrated using mean and diastole pressure to improve the prognostic value.
